title: ELF: Efficient Logic Synthesis by Pruning Redundancy in Refactoring
problem: Logic optimization via refactoring incurs high computational cost; conventional cut-based refactoring fails to improve circuit 98% of the time on average, wasting computation.
motivation: High failure rate in refactoring operations (98%) indicates opportunity to avoid expensive resynthesis operations through intelligent filtering.
method: ELF uses a machine-learning classifier to preemptively prune unsuccessful cut candidates before expensive resynthesis operations. Classifier predicts which cuts are unlikely to yield improvements, eliminating wasted computation. Applies to ABC logic synthesis framework's refactor operator.
key_novelty: ML-based cut pruning to eliminate redundant refactoring operations before resynthesis.
contributions: Classifier-based cut pruning reducing computational waste in refactor operator
3.9x speedup vs state-of-the-art ABC refactor implementation
Demonstrated on EPFL benchmark suite and 10 large industrial designs
limitations: Evaluation limited to refactor operator; applicability to other logic optimization operators (rewrite, restructure) not explored.
primary_theme: ML-accelerated logic synthesis via cut pruning
